meta.tagline: The easygoing city of Byzantium, the waterfront and long tables

overview.title: Welcome to Thessaloniki
overview.intro: Thessaloniki is a port city that shrugs at Athens' hurry: the waterfront invites kilometers of walking, the White Tower watches the sea, and the Ottoman lanes of the upper town, Ano Poli, climb toward the walls. Rome's Rotunda, Byzantium's UNESCO-listed churches, the Ottoman hamams and bedesten all fit into a single walk — and the house where Atatürk was born stands on one of these streets. But what makes Thessaloniki itself is not the stones, it's the rhythm: coffee is drunk long, tables rise late, nobody checks the clock. Its title as Greece's gastronomic capital is no accident.

local_word.definition: The Greek word for 'relax, don't force it, let it flow': Thessaloniki's factory setting. Coffee takes two hours? Halara. Bus is late? Halara. In this city, hurry counts as bad manners — put your watch in your pocket and switch to halara mode.

rules.title: Drink your coffee at Thessaloniki speed
rules.description: Order a frappé or freddo espresso and allow at least an hour: here coffee is not a drink but a way of sitting. No one moves you along and the bill never comes unasked — watching the sea over a waterfront coffee is the city's official sport.

rules.title: Climb to the upper town and see the city from the walls
rules.description: Ano Poli is the Ottoman fabric that survived the great fire: bay-windowed houses, narrow lanes, stone fountains. From the Trigonion Tower at sunset the whole gulf lies at your feet — walk up, and come down through the side alleys.

rules.title: Surrender to the meze culture
rules.description: The Thessaloniki table is built on sharing: order ouzo or tsipouro and the mezes arrive alongside, plates set in the middle. No main course is required — four or five mezes, a carafe and long conversation is the complete formula of a Thessaloniki evening.

tip.label: The Thessaloniki philosophy
tip.text: Keep the list short and the table long: bougatsa in the morning, waterfront at noon, meze at night — coffee ties it all together. Thessaloniki is not toured, it is lived; your best plan is to loosen the plan.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The center is walkable and the new metro carries the main artery; the waterfront, meanwhile, is the city's finest 'transit line' — on foot.

items.title: Arriving from the airport
items.description: Thessaloniki Airport is 30–40 minutes from the center: the X1 bus runs day and night and connects to the metro. Taxis run a fixed tariff — the practical choice for late-night landings.

items.title: The new metro
items.description: Thessaloniki's driverless metro runs beneath the main street: at Venizelou station an ancient road excavation is displayed under glass — the stop itself is like a museum. The center–station–university line covers a visitor's needs.

items.title: A walkable center
items.description: From Aristotelous Square to the White Tower, from Ladadika to the Rotunda, everything is walking distance: the waterfront is flat, Ano Poli is uphill. Comfortable shoes + halara pace = the ideal Thessaloniki walk.

items.title: City buses
items.description: For those skipping the Ano Poli climb, buses ascend to the walls; the coastal lines stretch to the eastern beaches. Buy tickets from machines or the app — drivers don't handle change.

items.title: Gulf boats
items.description: Excursion boats tour the gulf from the waterfront: on some you buy a drink instead of a ticket and the deck is yours. The sunset sailing is the most pleasant way to see the White Tower from the sea.

callout.label: Waterfront tip
callout.text: The full waterfront is one unbroken walk from the White Tower to the Concert Hall: start half an hour before sunset, pause at the Umbrellas sculpture, and settle into a waterfront cafe on the way back. This route is Thessaloniki's finest 'public transport'.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: The choice is a choice of rhythm: Ladadika at the foot of the nightlife, the practicality of the square, or the walled calm of Ano Poli.

local_word.definition: The aimless evening seaside stroll: the sacred ritual of Greek daily life — the word crossed into Turkish too, as 'volta atmak'. The Thessaloniki volta happens on the waterfront: everyone is there, nobody hurries. Dinner is considered earned only after the volta.

items.name: Ladadika
items.description: The old oil-warehouse quarter is now taverna and bar country: colorful facades, cobblestones, late-night music. Next to the port and the center — for those who want the nightlife at their doorstep.

items.name: Aristotelous and the center
items.description: Hotels around the grand square: waterfront, market and metro at hand. A balanced base for wandering everywhere on foot and returning to a square-side coffee at night.

items.name: Ano Poli
items.description: The upper town within the walls: bay-windowed houses, stone lanes, guesthouses with gulf views. It demands a climb, but repays with morning silence and sunset views.

items.name: Around Valaoritou
items.description: Boutique hotels and rooftop bars in old merchant buildings: calm by day, lively by night. Walking distance to the center and Ladadika, prices reasonable.

items.name: Kalamaria
items.description: The established district of the eastern shore: a marina, seaside cafes and fish tavernas. Linked to the center by bus — for living Thessaloniki like a local, at coastal rhythm.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Thessaloniki keeps its table set in all four seasons; spring and autumn belong to the waterfront walk, summer to beach escapes, November to the film festival.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Waterfront Spring
items.subtitle: Spring · Mild volta evenings, open-air tables
items.description: The waterfront volta is at its sweetest setting: mild air, tables spilling onto the streets, the Ano Poli slopes climbed in cool comfort. Tourist crowds are light — the city opens itself to you at local tempo.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: On a May evening start your volta at the White Tower and catch the sunset at the Umbrellas sculpture: the light fractures in its wires and the waterfront turns orange. Both the photograph and the dinner table open at this hour.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Heat and the Halkidiki Gate
items.subtitle: Summer · Hot city noons, beach escapes
items.description: Summer noon is hot and the city flows to the beach: Halkidiki's turquoise coves are an hour away. In the evening the waterfront cools and the rooftop bars open — the ideal season for a city-plus-beach double.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: In August some Thessalonians go on holiday and some family tavernas close: if gastronomy is your goal, skip mid-August. If you come, build the program on morning and evening and give noon to museums and coffee.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Festival and Harvest
items.subtitle: Autumn · Trade fair, film festival, full tavernas
items.description: September's international fair and November's film festival fill the city: tavernas celebrate the harvest and the sea is still warm. This is Thessaloniki at its most Thessaloniki — table and culture at the same seat.

callout.label: November tip
callout.text: In festival week the port warehouses become cinemas: buy a ticket, then sit down to meze in Ladadika after the film. The city's intellectual side and its appetite meet on the same night.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Chestnuts and Warm Tavernas
items.subtitle: Winter · Chestnut smoke, crowded indoor tavernas
items.description: Winter moves Thessaloniki indoors: tavernas fill, chestnuts roast on street corners, bougatsa steam fogs the shop windows. The Vardaris wind can bite — keep plans flexible and coats thick. Museums and churches are toured in peace in winter.

callout.label: December tip
callout.text: On a cold winter morning take a hot bougatsa from the bakery and walk to the Rotunda: inside it is dim, silent and nearly empty. Winter Thessaloniki means Byzantium without the crowds — and whoever gets cold warms up with tsipouro in a taverna.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Thessaloniki is Greece's culinary capital: the recipes of Izmir and Istanbul migrants, the Aegean's fish and Macedonia's bounty at one table.

local_word.definition: Custard cream (or cheese, or minced meat) between tissue-thin pastry layers: the official opening of a Thessaloniki morning. Cut from the tray, dusted with icing sugar and cinnamon. A Thessalonian is loyal to their bougatsa master with neighborhood devotion — the 'best bougatsa' debate is this city's national sport.

items.name: Bougatsa
items.description: Hot from the morning oven: the cream version with cinnamon and icing sugar, the cheese version at a salty setting. Standing at the counter or at a small table with coffee — this is the only correct way to say good morning to Thessaloniki.

items.name: The tsipouro and meze order
items.description: At a tsipouradiko, order a small bottle of tsipouro and let the mezes arrive on their own: each new bottle opens a new plate. Octopus, sardines, fava, pickles — the table builds slowly and the conversation stretches.
items.tag: Tsipouradiko style · a plate per bottle

items.name: Gyros and souvlaki
items.description: The Thessaloniki gyros is more generous and more ambitious than Athens': warm pita, fries tucked inside, tzatziki in abundance. The midnight standing classic — say 'ap'ola' and they load it with everything.

items.name: The fish taverna table
items.description: The gulf's sardines, grilled octopus and shrimp saganaki: in the tavernas of Kalamaria and behind the port. With horta (boiled greens) and lemon alongside — both shores of the Aegean meet on one plate.

items.name: Trigona Panoramatos
items.description: The cream-filled crisp cone invented in the Panorama district: cold custard piped into syrup-soaked pastry. Found downtown too, but pilgrims climb to Panorama — one is never enough.

items.name: Frappé and freddo culture
items.description: Greece is the homeland of iced coffee and its throne is in Thessaloniki: the frappé is whipped, the freddo espresso shaken. It lasts two hours at a waterfront table — nobody stares; everyone is doing the same work.
items.tag: Iced coffee throne · two hours long

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: In Thessaloniki you don't need a tourist menu because everywhere is already good — still, the measure is this: a taverna full of locals, a handwritten menu, a waiter who names the day's fish. The little tavernas inside the Modiano and Kapani markets are the city's most honest tables.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the White Tower; these six are the hidden addresses that open Thessaloniki's layers.

items.name: Trigonion Tower terrace
items.description: From the bastion at the top of Ano Poli the whole city and gulf lie at your feet: at sunset, local youth gather with thermoses and guitars. Thessaloniki's best view is free — bring something along and sit on the stone.

items.name: Atatürk House Museum
items.description: The pink house in the garden of the Turkish Consulate: the rooms where Mustafa Kemal was born, original furnishings and documents. Passport or ID required at the entrance — for Turkish visitors, Thessaloniki's most emotional stop.

items.name: The Kapani market tables
items.description: Small tavernas squeezed between the stalls of the city's oldest market: a table beside the fish crates, the day's freshest on the plate. The market's noise is the soundtrack — go at noon; it closes by evening.

items.name: The Rotunda
items.description: Galerius' 1700-year-old round mausoleum, once church and once mosque: gold mosaics in the dome, a single minaret at its side. All of Thessaloniki's layers in one building — the inside outshines the outside.

items.name: Around the Bit Bazaar
items.description: A courtyard of antique dealers and old record shops that turns into little ouzo tables by late afternoon: old Thessaloniki photographs, gramophones, prayer beads. Haggling allowed, hurry forbidden — the treasure hunter's corner.

items.name: Eptapyrgio (Yedi Kule)
items.description: The fortress at the very top of the walls, known by its Ottoman name Yedi Kule: a prison for many years, today a silent viewpoint. Above even Ano Poli, the city's least-known wall walk starts here.

callout.label: Layer strategy
callout.text: Tour Thessaloniki vertically: the shore layer in the morning (waterfront + White Tower), the market layer at noon (Kapani + Modiano + bedesten), the Byzantine layer in the afternoon (Agios Dimitrios + Rotunda), the wall layer at dusk (Ano Poli + Trigonion). From sea level to the ramparts — the city grows older as you climb.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Thessaloniki is an honest table city; still, the tourist's path crosses a few classic games — know these four.

items.name: The waterfront's photo menus
items.description: Some sea-view terraces run on photo menus and 'tourist specials': the price carries a view tax and the kitchen is mediocre.
items.instead: Drink your coffee on the waterfront but set your table a street or two inland: Ladadika's side lanes and the market tavernas give twice the flavor for the same money. A handwritten menu is a good sign.

items.name: The airport taxi tariff game
items.description: Despite a fixed tariff, some drivers inflate the number with 'night rates' or 'luggage surcharges'.
items.instead: Learn the official fixed fare beforehand and confirm it as you board; the X1 bus plus metro combination is cheap and quick. Ride apps also show a fixed price.

items.name: Climbing Ano Poli at noon heat
items.description: The trio of slope, cobblestones and July sun turns a pleasure walk into an ordeal; whoever reaches the top has no strength left for the view.
items.instead: Climb Ano Poli in the morning cool or two hours before sunset; or take the bus up and walk down. The Trigonion sunset plan always wins.

items.name: 'Handmade' souvenir windows
items.description: On the tourist streets, mass-produced evil-eye beads and imported goods labeled 'Greek handicraft' sell at workshop prices.
items.instead: Buy from the Bit Bazaar's antique dealers and the spice and olive-oil merchants around Modiano: a shopkeeper who tells the product's story quotes an honest price too. A Macedonian wine also makes a fine gift.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Thessaloniki the compass of a good experience is the local: the local's coffee, the local's taverna, the local's hour. When in doubt, choose the place where the crowd speaks Greek — in this city, living like a local is the best way of being a tourist.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From bougatsa to volta — a Thessaloniki day

steps.title: Bougatsa morning
steps.description: Hot cream bougatsa from the bakery, cinnamon on top: first coffee alongside. You've started the day Thessaloniki-style.

steps.title: Waterfront and the White Tower
steps.description: Walk from Aristotelous down to the sea, along the waterfront to the White Tower: climb it and see the gulf from above. Stretch on to the Umbrellas sculpture.

steps.title: Market lunch at Kapani
steps.description: A taverna table among the market stalls: the day's fish, fava, a small tsipouro. Thessaloniki's most honest noon.

steps.title: The Byzantine and Roman layer
steps.description: The crypt silence of Agios Dimitrios, then the gold mosaics of the Rotunda: two buildings, seventeen centuries.

steps.title: Ano Poli and Trigonion sunset
steps.description: Climb through the upper town's bay-windowed lanes to the walls: sit on the stone at Trigonion and watch the gulf turn orange.

steps.title: Ladadika evening
steps.description: The meze order on the taverna lanes: octopus, horta, a carafe of wine. The closing volta on the waterfront — with the lights on the water.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Waterfront, layers and the gulf — the full Thessaloniki

steps.title: Classic Thessaloniki
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: bougatsa, the waterfront, a Kapani table, the Rotunda, Ano Poli, Ladadika.

steps.title: Memory and museums
steps.description: Morning at the Atatürk House (bring ID) and the market hamams and bedesten; meze at Modiano for lunch; one of the Archaeological or Byzantine museums in the afternoon; sunset at a Valaoritou rooftop + ouzo around the Bit Bazaar.

steps.title: Gulf or Halkidiki escape
steps.description: In summer, a morning bus to Halkidiki's coves — a turquoise break; otherwise a gulf boat + the Kalamaria marina and a fish taverna. Climb to Panorama for trigona on the way back; a farewell volta to the White Tower, and the last frappé at a waterfront table.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Greek and Turkish have fed from the same table for centuries; these five phrases open doors and tables in Thessaloniki.

items.meaning: Good morning / good day — greet the baker and the tower clerk alike
Thank you — looks hard, becomes reflex within three days
Cheers! — as the tsipouro glasses rise; make eye contact
Enjoy your meal — the waiter says it setting down the plate; say it to your table too
Come / come on / no way — the multi-purpose exclamation of Greek daily life

checklist.completion_message: Yamas! You've lived the city of the waterfront and the layers the way it deserves!
